newsitem.title: UK: London council says MGAM funds still under review.
newsitem.headline: London council says MGAM funds still under review.

text.p: London's Westminster City Council said on Thursday it was continuing to review its funds invested with Morgan Grenfell Asset Management following this week's suspension of fund manager Nicola Horlick.

"Our position is unchanged. We are continuing to monitor the situation," a council spokeswoman told Reuters. Last October the council, which has pension funds totalling around 400 million stg, said it would look at alternative managers following last year's revelations of misvaluations at three MGAM funds.
Westminster was asked by elected members of the council at the time to start looking at the possibility of using alternative fund managers to MGAM. This process is continuing, the spokeswoman said.
Horlick, head of MGAM's UK pension fund business, was suspended on Tuesday by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG), the investment banking arm of Germany's Deutsche Bank.
DMG said it had suspended Horlick "pending the outcome of an internal investigation which will look at a potential breach of her contract".
Banking sources said the suspension followed talks between Horlick and Dutch bank ABN AMRO and overtures made by Horlick to members of her team to move to the Dutch firm.
